statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: In mouse embryonic stem cells, AGO1 in turn represses the expression of AGO2.
statements.evidence: These recent findings raise the question of whether and how these two AGOs are mutually regulated in mESCs.
statements.note: The abstract raises the question of mutual regulation but reports only that AGO2 represses AGO1; it says nothing about AGO1 acting on AGO2.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Two of the four Argonaute proteins found in mammals, AGO1 and AGO2, are expressed in mouse embryonic stem cells.
statements.evidence: Of the four AGOs in mammals, AGO1 and AGO2 are expressed in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs).
statements.note: The abstract names AGO1 and AGO2 as the two of the four mammalian AGOs that are expressed in mESCs.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study showed that AGO2 represses expression of AGO1 mRNA by acting through a let-7 microRNA binding site in the AGO1 3' UTR.
statements.evidence: using loss-of-function and gain-of-function approaches, we show that AGO2 represses the expression of AGO1 mRNA via a conserved let-7-microRNA-binding site in its 3' UTR
statements.note: Loss- and gain-of-function experiments showed that AGO2 represses AGO1 mRNA via a let-7 binding site in its 3' UTR.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: When the let-7 site was mutated in the endogenous AGO1 gene, AGO2 no longer repressed AGO1 mRNA and mESCs were impaired in exiting pluripotency.
statements.evidence: Mutating this binding site at the endogenous locus abolishes the AGO2-mediated repression of AGO1 mRNA and compromises the exit pluripotency of mESCs.
statements.note: Mutating the binding site at the endogenous locus abolished AGO2-mediated repression of AGO1 and compromised the mESCs' exit from pluripotency.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Although they come from a single locus, the lncRNA Rncr3 and its embedded microRNA miR124a-1 play separate and opposite roles.
statements.evidence: identify independent and opposing roles for two neural-specific and differentially expressed non-coding RNAs derived from the same locus: the evolutionarily conserved lncRNA Rncr3 and the embedded microRNA miR124a-1
statements.note: The abstract reports independent and opposing roles for Rncr3 and the embedded miR124a-1, both derived from the same locus.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Mutations in MeCP2 that block its binding to Rncr3 underlie the neurological symptoms of Rett syndrome.
statements.evidence: Thus, miRNA processing is controlled by lncRNA m 5 C methylation along with the defined m 5 C epitranscriptomic RNA reader protein MeCP2 to coordinate brain development.
statements.note: The abstract ties MeCP2's reading of methylated Rncr3 to normal brain development but mentions no disease, patient mutations or Rett syndrome.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Processing of miR124a is suppressed by MeCP2, which recruits PTBP1 so that DROSHA-DGCR8 cannot reach the RNA.
statements.evidence: MeCP2 directly binds cytosine-methylated Rncr3 through previously unrecognized lysine residues and suppresses miR124a processing by recruiting PTBP1 to block access of DROSHA-DGCR8.
statements.note: The abstract states that MeCP2 suppresses miR124a processing by recruiting PTBP1, which blocks DROSHA-DGCR8 access.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In Rncr3, exons 2 and 3 carry cytosine methylation and are bound by MeCP2, which limits expression of the miR124a located in exon 4.
statements.evidence: Rncr3 conserved exons 2/3 are cytosine methylated and bound by methyl-CpG binding protein MeCP2, which restricts expression of miR124a embedded in exon 4
statements.note: The abstract reports that methylated Rncr3 exons 2/3 are bound by MeCP2, which restricts expression of the miR124a embedded in exon 4.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: miR-2b-1 acts in the developing nervous system to shape the emergence of embryonic movement in Drosophila.
statements.evidence: we define that miR-2b-1 influences the emergence of embryonic movement by exerting actions in the developing nervous system
statements.note: Several approaches, including neural optical imaging, showed that miR-2b-1 influences movement emergence through actions in the developing nervous system.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Restoring miR-2b-1 in selected cells of null mutants indicated that it affects movement onset via sensory elements of the embryonic circuit, not the motor domain.
statements.evidence: suggest that miR-2b-1 affects the emergence of movement through effects in sensory elements of the embryonic circuitry, rather than in the motor domain
statements.note: Cell-specific reconstitution in a null mutant background pointed to sensory elements, rather than the motor domain, as where miR-2b-1 acts.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Drosophila embryos lacking miR-2b-1 start moving later than wild-type embryos.
statements.evidence: using this system, discover that the Drosophila miRNA miR-2b-1 plays a role in the emergence of movement
statements.note: The abstract says miR-2b-1 plays a role in the emergence of movement but never states whether its absence makes movement begin earlier or later.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A previously uncharacterised chloride channel gene, termed Motor, is evolutionarily conserved and is a target that mechanistically links miR-2b-1 to movement onset.
statements.evidence: we identify a previously uncharacterised (but evolutionarily conserved) chloride channel encoding gene - which we term Mo vement Modula tor ( Motor ) - as a genetic target that mechanistically links miR-2b-1 to the onset of movement
statements.note: The abstract identifies Motor, an uncharacterised but evolutionarily conserved chloride channel gene, as the target linking miR-2b-1 to movement onset.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Arabidopsis plants with mir157c mutations flowered sooner under short days and had altered inflorescence leaves, whereas mir156ac mutations did not speed flowering.
statements.evidence: CRISPR-induced mir157c mutations but not mir156ac mutations accelerated flowering under SDs, and altered inflorescence leaf morphology.
statements.note: Under short days, CRISPR mir157c mutations, but not mir156ac mutations, accelerated flowering and altered inflorescence leaf morphology.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The age-dependent decline of miR156 and miR157 in Arabidopsis is driven by sugar signals produced in the leaves.
statements.evidence: In Arabidopsis, age-dependent reduction in the related microRNAs miR156 and miR157 controls transitions from juvenile to adult vegetative phase and from adult to reproductive phase.
statements.note: The abstract describes the age-dependent reduction of miR156 and miR157 and what it controls, but says nothing about the signal that causes it.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In RISCs from shoot apices of plants undergoing the floral transition, miR157 is present at higher levels than miR156.
statements.evidence: We show that in shoot apices, levels of miR156 in RNA-induced silencing complexes (RISCs) decline more rapidly than those of miR157, so that miR157 is more abundant than miR156 in RISCs of older plants undergoing floral transition and inflorescence development.
statements.note: Because RISC-bound miR156 declines faster in shoot apices, miR157 becomes more abundant than miR156 in RISCs of older plants at floral transition.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mutating mir157c in Arabis alpina, a perennial relative of Arabidopsis, also made the plants flower early.
statements.evidence: mir157c mutations also caused early flowering in Arabis alpina, a perennial relative of Arabidopsis
statements.note: The abstract reports early flowering in Arabis alpina mir157c mutants and takes it as evidence that this repression of flowering is evolutionarily conserved.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: MYRF-1 activity is needed to license a developmental checkpoint on which growth and successful ecdysis depend.
statements.evidence: we show that MYRF-1 activity is also required to license a developmental checkpoint essential for growth and successful ecdysis
statements.note: The abstract states that MYRF-1 activity is required to license a checkpoint essential for growth and successful ecdysis.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Light-dark cycles entrain the MYRF-1/LIN-42 developmental timer, tying it to the circadian clock.
statements.evidence: Here, we identify a developmental timer composed of the transcription factor MYRF-1 and the PERIOD-like repressor LIN-42 that operates synchronously across all somatic tissues.
statements.note: The abstract calls LIN-42 PERIOD-like but reports nothing about light, circadian rhythms or entrainment of the timer.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: MYRF-1 binds regulatory elements upstream of heterochronic microRNA genes and triggers one transcriptional pulse per developmental stage, phase-locked across tissues.
statements.evidence: MYRF-1 binds conserved regulatory elements upstream of heterochronic microRNA genes and drives once-per-stage transcriptional pulses that are phase-locked across tissues
statements.note: The abstract reports that MYRF-1 drives once-per-stage transcriptional pulses of heterochronic microRNA genes that are phase-locked across tissues.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: When newly synthesised LIN-42 associates directly with MYRF-1, MYRF-1 nuclear residence and transcriptional activity are reduced, restricting the amplitude and duration of each pulse.
statements.evidence: Newly synthesized LIN-42 directly associates with MYRF-1, limiting its nuclear residence and transcriptional activity and thereby constraining the amplitude and duration of each pulse.
statements.note: Newly made LIN-42 binds MYRF-1 and limits its nuclear residence and activity, which constrains the amplitude and duration of each pulse.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In C. elegans larvae lacking LIN28, only two LIN28-bound RNAs, lin-46 mRNA and let-7 miRNA, changed in level; the other bound transcripts did not.
statements.evidence: loss of LIN28 leaves the levels of most LIN28-bound transcripts unchanged. The only exceptions are the lin-46 mRNA and the let-7 miRNA.
statements.note: Loss of LIN28 left most bound transcripts unchanged, with lin-46 mRNA and let-7 miRNA as the only two exceptions.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Removing lin-46 and let-7 in lin-28 null animals completely abolished their precocious heterochronic phenotypes, producing the retarded phenotypes of lin-46; let-7 double mutants.
statements.evidence: lin-28; lin-46; let-7 triple mutant animals exhibit complete suppression of the lin-28(0) precocious heterochronic phenotypes and recapitulate the retarded lin-46; let-7 double mutant phenotypes
statements.note: Triple mutants fully suppress the lin-28(0) precocious phenotypes and recapitulate the retarded lin-46; let-7 double mutant phenotypes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Simultaneously overexpressing lin-46 and let-7 reproduces the phenotype caused by LIN28 loss.
statements.evidence: Conversely, simultaneous overexpression of lin-46 and let-7 mimics LIN28 loss.
statements.note: The abstract states that overexpressing lin-46 and let-7 together mimics LIN28 loss.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: C. elegans larvae lacking LIN28 develop at a faster tempo than wild-type larvae.
statements.evidence: Unexpectedly, LIN28 controls not only cell identity but also the tempo of development, using the same two targets.
statements.note: The abstract says LIN28 controls developmental tempo but does not say whether losing LIN28 speeds development up or slows it down.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Structures were solved for DCL4 bound to RNA in a dicing-competent state and for the DCL4-DRB4-RNA complex in a state preceding dicing.
statements.evidence: Here we determined the structures of the DCL4-RNA complex in a dicing-competent conformation and the DCL4-DRB4-RNA complex in a pre-dicing conformation.
statements.note: The abstract reports structures of DCL4-RNA in a dicing-competent conformation and DCL4-DRB4-RNA in a pre-dicing conformation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Because a DCL4-specific loop places DCL4's second dsRNA-binding domain and DRB4 at a distal site on the substrate, the complex favours longer RNAs.
statements.evidence: A DCL4-specific loop locates the second double-stranded RNA binding domain of DCL4 and DRB4 to a distal position of the substrate RNA, yielding a preference for long RNA substrates.
statements.note: Positioning of the second dsRBD and DRB4 at a distal site by the DCL4-specific loop yields a preference for long RNA substrates.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: DCL4 sets siRNA length by spanning 21 nucleotides of RNA between its PAZ domain and its RNase III domains.
statements.evidence: DCL4 measures 21 nucleotides along RNA between its PAZ and RNase III domains to determine the product siRNA length.
statements.note: The abstract states that DCL4 measures 21 nucleotides between its PAZ and RNase III domains to determine siRNA length.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Mutating the DCL4-specific loop impairs post-transcriptional gene silencing in Arabidopsis plants.
statements.evidence: Our studies demonstrate the molecular basis of substrate recognition, length measurement and long RNA preference by the DCL4-DRB4 complex for 21-nucleotide siRNA biogenesis in plants.
statements.note: The abstract explains the loop's structural role but reports no loop mutants and no measurement of gene silencing in plants.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: C. elegans lacking every member of the miR-51 family die as embryos.
statements.evidence: We reveal the molecular function of its C. elegans homolog, the miR-51 family.
statements.note: The abstract reports dose-dependent control of morphogenesis and the family's targets but says nothing about survival or embryonic lethality.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The miR-51 family, the C. elegans counterpart of miR-100, controls morphogenesis in a dose-dependent way by regulating genes for cell signalling, adhesion and migration.
statements.evidence: This family acts in a dose-dependent manner to control morphogenesis by regulating several genes involved in cell signaling, adhesion, and migration
statements.note: The abstract states that the miR-51 family controls morphogenesis dose-dependently by regulating signaling, adhesion and migration genes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Having emerged in the last shared ancestor of eumetazoans, miR-100 remains conserved throughout much of the animal kingdom.
statements.evidence: A single miRNA, miR-100, arose in the last common eumetazoan ancestor and is widely conserved across animals.
statements.note: The abstract states that miR-100 arose in the last common eumetazoan ancestor and is widely conserved across animals.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Some of the miR-51 family's target genes are predicted to be conserved microRNA targets in vertebrates too.
statements.evidence: Some of these targets are also predicted to be conserved targets across vertebrates.
statements.note: The abstract reports that some miR-51 family targets are also predicted to be conserved targets across vertebrates.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Manipulating miR-317, or treating aphids with JH, changed winged offspring production but caused no detectable wing malformations.
statements.evidence: Manipulation of miR-317 or JH treatment altered winged offspring production without causing detectable wing malformations
statements.note: The abstract reports that miR-317 manipulation or JH treatment altered winged offspring production without detectable wing malformations.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Two hormone-responsive microRNA cascades converge on one shared target, glycogen phosphorylase, with each regulating a distinct phase of aphid wing plasticity.
statements.evidence: Here, we identified two hormone-responsive miRNA cascades that converged on a common target, glycogen phosphorylase ( GP ), to regulate distinct phases of wing plasticity.
statements.note: The abstract identifies two hormone-responsive miRNA cascades that converge on GP to regulate distinct phases of wing plasticity.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Poor host-plant quality induces winged aphid offspring through the same JH, miR-317 and GP pathway that responds to crowding.
statements.evidence: Under high density, JH triggers RRP44 (exosome complex exonuclease RRP44 )-mediated depletion of cytoplasmic pre-miR-317, reducing mature miR-317 and relieving GP repression, which in turn promotes winged offspring production.
statements.note: The abstract links the JH, miR-317 and GP pathway only to high population density; host-plant cues are not examined.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Knocking down glycogen phosphorylase impaired glycogen breakdown and resulted in lower ATP levels.
statements.evidence: GP knockdown impaired glycogen breakdown and lowered ATP levels
statements.note: The abstract states that GP knockdown impaired glycogen breakdown and lowered ATP levels.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Fifteen miRNAs changed pigmentation in opposite ways when ectopically expressed versus inhibited, and computational tools found candidate targets for them among 93 known pigmentation genes.
statements.evidence: For each of the 15 miRNAs with opposing effects in the gain- and loss-of-function screens, computational tools identified possible targets among 93 genes previously reported to affect adult pigmentation.
statements.note: The abstract reports 15 miRNAs with opposing effects in the two screens, with possible targets identified among 93 pigmentation genes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Ebony, bric-a-brac 1 and bric-a-brac 2, whose 3' UTRs mediated regulation by miR-8 in cell culture, all lead to reduced development of black pigment.
statements.evidence: we found that one of these miRNAs (miR-8) was able to regulate gene expression through 3' UTR sequences from at least 3 pigmentation genes: ebony, bric-a-brac 1, and bric-a-brac 2. All 3 of these genes reduce the development of black pigments
statements.note: miR-8 regulated expression through the 3' UTRs of ebony, bric-a-brac 1 and bric-a-brac 2, and all three genes reduce black pigment development.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: miR-8 contributes to differences in body pigmentation between Drosophila species.
statements.evidence: These data show that miRNAs are developmental regulators of body pigmentation, which could also allow them to contribute to pigmentation divergence, as has been shown for miR-193 in butterflies.
statements.note: The abstract only raises the possibility that miRNAs contribute to pigmentation divergence, citing miR-193 in butterflies; it shows no species differences for miR-8.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Of 166 miRNAs expressed ectopically in a dorsal stripe of developing flies, 48 were each able on their own to change pigmentation.
statements.evidence: We found that 48 of 166 miRNAs ectopically expressed in a stripe along the dorsal side of developing flies were each sufficient to affect pigmentation.
statements.note: In the gain-of-function screen, 48 of the 166 ectopically expressed miRNAs were each sufficient to affect pigmentation.
